cohort: Patients with pre-labor rupture of membranes (PROM) at term and unfavorable Bishop scores who underwent induction of labor.
finding: Oral misoprostol for induction of labor in term PROM resulted in a lower rate of vaginal delivery within 24 hours and longer induction-to-delivery duration compared to IV Oxytocin, but reduced labor ward admission time and did not increase maternal or neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Oral misoprostol led to a reduced chance of vaginal delivery within 24 hours compared to IV Oxytocin, especially in nulliparous women, but the overall rate within 48 hours was similar, and it did not increase the risk of cesarean delivery or other maternal/neonatal complications.
